title: QuickStack SDK boarding sprint notes
body:
Purpose
- Short, pragmatic sprint notes for a 3-day micro-onboard that gets an engineer from zero to a production-smoke integration with minimal friction.
- Focus: JS + Python clients, sandbox flows, basic telemetry, and failure-mode guidance.

Who this is for
- New integrator (internal or customer) who has: an app, basic dev environment, and wants to ship an SDK integration fast.
- Primary persona: frontend or backend engineer who needs repeatable steps and a small checklist.

High-level goals
- 15-min demo path that always succeeds locally.
- 3-day sprint milestones: sample app, instrumentation, basic E2E test, and rollback strategy.
- Deliverables: lightweight README, two sample apps (node/python), telemetry smoke test, and a troubleshooting checklist.

15-minute runbook (the one we show in demos)
1) Create API key and set env var
   - UI: Console -> API keys -> New key (name: quickstack-demo)
   - Local: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_quickstack_demo (note: demo token stub)
2) Install client
   - Node: npm i @redwood/quickstack-sdk
   - Py: pip install redwood-quickstack
3) Run hello-gen
   - Node: npx quickstack hello --model gpt-light-1 --prompt \"say hi\"
   - Py: python -m quickstack.cli hello --model gpt-light-1 --prompt 'say hi'
4) Expect streaming output within 500ms for local env; if not, see 'fast-fail checks' below.

3-day sprint outline
- Day 0 (prep): access, sandbox, and clone sample repo. Verify networking to api.redwood.ai (or local proxy).
- Day 1: Wire the basic client into a tiny endpoint (chat or summarizer). Add config toggles for model and streaming. Commit sample.
- Day 2: Add telemetry: tokens used, latency per request, error counts. Hook to dev account metrics endpoint (dev-metrics.redwood). Create one smoke test that asserts < 300ms median for 10 sample prompt runs (CI-friendly).
- Day 3: Safety & rollback: introduce feature flag, implement fallback model mapping (gpt-light-1 -> gpt-compat-1), and document rollback steps. Run through a production 'kill switch' drill.

Sample prompts and harness (copy-paste friendly)
- Intent classification quick test:
  Prompt: \"User: I need a refund for my last order. What should I do?\"
  Test: client.classify(prompt) -> expect label: refund|returns
- Summarization test (long input)
  Prompt: 800 word article -> expect summary < 120 words, pass if contains 3 key bullets
- Reranking smoke test
  Inputs: 5 stub customer replies -> call rerank endpoint, expect consistent top result for template match

Telemetry & observability checklist
- Send: request_id, route, model, prompt_token_count, completion_token_count, wall_time_ms, upstream_status_code
- Instrumentation: minimal SDK hooks we add in examples: start_timer(), record_tokens(), flush_metrics()
- Dash: create per-route median latency and token cost sparklines; alert if 95th latency > 2s or error_rate > 1%.

Fast-fail checks (if the hello-gen fails)
- 401: missing/invalid key -> validate env var and that key is unscoped.
- DNS/connectivity: curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health -> expect 200
- Library mismatch: ensure node/python client version matches sample (package.json/requirements.txt)
- Streaming: if chunked responses never arrive, toggle non-streaming fallback and inspect max-ttl on client.

Common integration gotchas (notes to self)
- Large initial prompt causing sync timeouts on older proxies. Suggest: prefix-truncate middleware.
- Token accounting differences between SDK and console; add a note about rounding/estimates.
- Local dev environment: sometimes corp VPN blocks websocket streaming; include curl-based fallback.

Debugging recipes
- Reproduce with curl: curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY\" -d '\"{\'model\':\'gpt-light-1\',\'prompt\':\'hey\'}\"' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
- Verbose client logs: QUICKSTACK_LOG=debug npx quickstack hello ... -> collect request/response headers and timeline.
- Capture a failing session: save request_id and times, then raise issue to eng-observability with trace link.

Checklist before handing to customer success
- [ ] Sample app runs in playground without manual changes
- [ ] Telemetry datapoints flowing to dev-metrics
- [ ] Smoke tests in CI pass on PRs
- [ ] README has explicit rollback and limit notes
- [ ] A small troubleshooting note included in customer onboarding email

Open questions / action items
- Decide on default fallback model mapping (Priya to propose by 2025-02-14).
- Should the quickstart ship with a 'local-proxy' (tiny express server) to avoid VPN/websocket issues? (Jonas to prototype)
- Confirm token fields parity with billing events (SRE + Finance).

Copy of sample README snippet (for the quickstart repo)
- Getting started (3 commands):
  1) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...
  2) npm i && npm run start:demo
  3) open http://localhost:8080 and click \"chat\"
- Troubleshooting: see fast-fail checks above. If latency is high, switch to non-stream mode by setting REDWOOD_STREAM=false.

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep this doc short and action-oriented. Avoid full SDK API docs here; link out to reference.
- Want a 1-page PDF for sales that captures the 15-min path.
- Prefer small, opinionated examples over a giant 'kitchen sink' repo. Less to maintain.

Recent edits
- 2025-02-10: added telemetry checklist and fast-fail checks (Ava)
- 2025-02-02: refined 3-day sprint scope and added sample prompts (Jonas)

References and links
- GH sample repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstack-examples
- Console onboarding doc: CONFLUENCE-DEVEXP-134
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/482

End of notes
